rationale: This is very close to the archived "Cash-Validated Intangible Turnover Improvement" (same 3-year cash-margin leg times an asset-turnover-improvement leg, here re-expressed as sales growth minus asset growth) with an intangible-intensity leg bolted on from "Cash-Funded Intangible Compounder," and the growth-spread leg is itself largely the well-known asset-growth/efficient-growth anomaly.

It reuses two legs from "Gross-Margin Floor Intangible Moat" but substitutes a genuinely different third leg — cash conversion of gross profit rather than accounting operating margin — which directly addresses the accrual-versus-cash validation question, though the oancf/(revt−cogs) ratio is unstable for low-gross-profit firms even after winsorization and the incremental content over the archived version is modest.

Two of three legs are identical to the archived "Intangible Overhead Discipline," with only the profitability leg swapped from oibdp/sale to DELTA(oancf)/at — a cosmetic substitution that does not diagnose why that signal delivered only a 2.2 t-alpha.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals — the goodwill-minus-internal-intangibles leg from "Acquired Intangible Cash Decay" spliced onto the margin-decay and sales-drawdown legs of "Goodwill Demand Drawdown" — and does nothing to resolve that family's persistent fmb_tstat/ls_talpha contradiction (near-zero cross-sectional slope with a large tail-driven spread alpha).

Fourth reuse of the same "intangible level × NEG cash/margin trend × NEG sales-vs-peak" template, and because the product is dominated by the two decay legs that already generate the archive's -3.5 to -4.8 t-alphas with near-zero FMB slopes, the swap of goodwill for identifiable intangibles is unlikely to produce economically distinct information.

The interest-burden leg is new to this archive and the acquisition-overhang-plus-debt-service mechanism is coherent, but the multiplicative NEG(oibdp/sale) leg means the signal will likely load heavily on generic low profitability (already in FF5 as RMW) and financial distress, so the incremental content beyond known anomalies is uncertain.
